1: # Instructions
2: 
3: Reparent a tree on a selected node.
4: 
5: A [tree][wiki-tree] is a special type of [graph][wiki-graph] where all nodes are connected but there are no cycles.
6: That means, there is exactly one path to get from one node to another for any pair of nodes.
7: 
8: This exercise is all about re-orientating a tree to see things from a different point of view.
9: For example family trees are usually presented from the ancestor's perspective:
10: 
11: ```text
12:     +------0------+
13:     |      |      |
14:   +-1-+  +-2-+  +-3-+
15:   |   |  |   |  |   |
16:   4   5  6   7  8   9
17: ```
18: 
19: But there is no inherent direction in a tree.
20: The same information can be presented from the perspective of any other node in the tree, by pulling it up to the root and dragging its relationships along with it.
21: So the same tree from 6's perspective would look like:
22: 
23: ```text
24:         6
25:         |
26:   +-----2-----+
27:   |           |
28:   7     +-----0-----+
29:         |           |
30:       +-1-+       +-3-+
31:       |   |       |   |
32:       4   5       8   9
33: ```
34: 
35: This lets us more simply describe the paths between two nodes.
36: So for example the path from 6-9 (which in the first tree goes up to the root and then down to a different leaf node) can be seen to follow the path 6-2-0-3-9.
37: 
38: This exercise involves taking an input tree and re-orientating it from the point of view of one of the nodes.
39:

41: [wiki-tree]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_(discrete_mathematics)

The spec is the Exercism "Point of View" exercise: reroot a tree at a given node (`FromPov`) and find the path between two nodes (`PathTo`). The tests compare trees structurally (children may be in any order) and return `nil` when a target doesn't exist.

I'll implement it by finding the root-to-target path, then rebuilding the tree bottom-up so each node on the path swaps its "child on the path" for the previously rebuilt subtree:

All tests pass. Implementation in `pov.go`:

- **`Tree`** now stores `value string` and `children []*Tree`; `New`, `Value`, and `Children` are straightforward accessors.
- **`FromPov`** does a DFS to find the root-to-target path (returns `nil` if the node doesn't exist), then rebuilds the tree bottom-up from the root: each node on the path keeps its off-path children and adopts the already-rebuilt subtree toward the target as a new child. The original tree is never mutated.
- **`PathTo`** reroots the tree at `from` via `FromPov`, then walks down from the new root to `to` — in a tree the unique path from root to `to` is exactly the answer. Returns `nil` if either node is missing.
